claim_policy.claims_from_operational_constraints: creating a new claim from operational_constraints is forbidden; operational_constraints may only bind an oracle for an already-provided required claim ID; in the conformance lane any extra claim fails the exact registered-ID rule; in the held-out lane decomposed claims follow the existing held-out policy and are never credited without a registered adapter

execution.command_sandbox_denial_policy: the exact Next.js 16 Turbopack internal-bind denial signature is blocked safe_execution_unavailable; raw argv is never rewritten and the claim remains unverified
execution.network: external denied; candidate build has all network denied; candidate servers are loopback-only; host-fixed browser blocks non-same-origin requests

next_build_policy.candidate_visible: next_version and safe_build_argv are exposed via executor_capabilities.next; a candidate command oracle whose argv equals safe_build_argv is executable, any other next build argv is policy_rejected
next_build_policy.detection: read node_modules/next/package.json version inside the frozen product workspace; record it in evidence
next_build_policy.unregistered: safe_execution_unavailable (blocked, claim stays unverified); never guess a flag
next_build_policy.verification: confirmed on 2026-08-27 against direct `node_modules/.bin/next build --help`: 14.2.35 package sha256 851ca2846050593b78eed7d371b530c8eb32935122e1e2fd5fc8fc6d49cb48dd has no --webpack option; 16.3.1 package sha256 dc243091ba95352bbc300be22c6561d24a19a1c0bd2c2cc85d2c5168767ea7b9 exposes --webpack; A9 unit fixtures cover both registered versions and an unregistered version

execution.per_oracle_port_binding: retained: each http/dom/interaction oracle's own setup.argv must contain its port as a distinct item; no cross-oracle port inference
execution.sandbox: candidate commands and candidate servers use macos_sandbox_exec
execution.server_policy: host-owned direct argv Next.js production build then start, selected by the detected product-workspace Next version (see next_build_policy); build network is denied, server is loopback-only, signals are limited to same-sandbox targets, no shell chaining, and selectors/read targets remain candidate-owned
execution.stage_resolution: effective stage is decided exactly once from the claim's intent-compatible origin before any workspace is selected; existing_fix_evidence and existing_investigation_binding execute against the product workspace and keep the origin stage (before/after/reproduce) inside the binding record; execution_snapshot_sha256 must equal the frozen hash of the workspace actually used
execution.unknown_flag_policy: scoped to registered Next.js build/start requests only: an unregistered Next build/start option is policy_rejected before execution and recorded; Python, pytest, and other direct argv continue to use the existing safety validator rather than a nonexistent global option allowlist; raw argv is never rewritten
